big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
consumes. -/
noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩

/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/

/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice

end AlgebraicGeometry

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartPair

/-!
# THE ATLAS IS CHART-PARAMETER HETEROGENEOUS — each chart may carry its own `n`

`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` establishes that at a chart index legal at parameter
`n` the coverage theorem's threshold is forced to equal `n`, and that at `n = g` the resulting
hypothesis is false.  Both that file and the review it adjudicates (I-0660) then reason about
"the" chart parameter, as though the atlas had one.

**It does not, and this file proves it.**  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
(`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) takes a family `f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf`
indexed by an arbitrary `ι`, with `X : ι → Scheme` and a *per-index* certificate
`hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`.  Nothing ties the `X i` together, so nothing ties
their chart parameters together either: `mixedParamChart` below builds such a family from a
per-index parameter `nn : ι → ℕ`, a per-index representation of `divFunctor C π (nn i)`, and a
per-index chart index legal *at that index's own parameter*.

## Why this matters, and it changes the shape of the residue

The `b = n` calibration is per-chart.  So the question "can coverage use DAT-0a's threshold?"
does not have to be answered uniformly: a point whose splitting field has threshold `b_L` can be
covered by *the chart whose parameter is `b_L.toNat`*, and a different point by a different
chart.  The I-0204 non-uniformity of `m` — no single exponent works for every fibre — is
therefore **not** an obstruction to the atlas; it is an argument for an atlas indexed by the
threshold, which is what a heterogeneous family is.

What this does **not** do, and the honest limit of the observation:

* it does not produce the representations.  `mixedParamChart` takes `rep i` as a hypothesis, one
  per parameter, and the divisor-representability lane supplies `divFunctor C π g` — a single
  parameter.  So the heterogeneous atlas is *admissible* but not yet *inhabited* beyond `n = g`;
* it does not discharge `IsChartUniv` at any index (still CERT-Σ-gated, `Pic0ChartPair.lean`);
* it says nothing about local surjectivity, which is DAT-B B-6 and is what would actually consume
  the freedom.

So the correct statement of the residue, refining `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s: **B-5's step 3
is a question about which parameters `divFunctor C π n` is representable at, not about
reconciling one parameter with one threshold.**  If representability is available only at `n = g`
then the slack must go into `Z` (and its legality is open, as recorded there); if it is available
at every `n`, coverage can be assembled chart-by-chart against each fibre's own threshold and the
`b = n` forcing is harmless.  That is a sharper question than either prior reading, and it is
addressed to the divRep lane rather than to this one.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamChart` — a chart family with a per-index chart parameter.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart` — its `hf` clause is exactly a
  per-index `IsChartUniv`, so heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamRepresentableBy` — such a family is admissible input to
  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  **This is the whole point**: the DAT-glue seam never sees a
  chart parameter.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

variable (C π) in
/-- **A chart family whose chart parameter varies with the index.**

Each index `i` carries its own degree parameter `nn i`, its own representing object `D i` of
`divFunctor C π (nn i)`, its own twist exponent `m i` and chart index `Z i` — the latter legal
*at `nn i`*, i.e. `deg_k (Z i) = (m i)·d₁ − nn i`, which is what `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`
requires for that index's chart value to land in `pic⁰`.

The construction is just `restrictChart` of `abelSigmaChart` applied pointwise; the content is
that it *typechecks*, i.e. that the target `pic0SigmaSheaf C` is parameter-free. -/
def mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
    yoneda.obj ((V i : Scheme.{u})) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
  restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)

variable (C π) in
/-- **Heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate**: the `hf` clause of a mixed-parameter
family is exactly a per-index `IsChartUniv`, by definition of both.

So a lane that can discharge CHART-U(c) *at one parameter* can discharge it index-by-index at
different parameters, with no additional compatibility between them — there is no coherence
condition across indices, because `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` imposes none. -/
theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
    (huniv : ∀ i, IsChartUniv C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i)) (i : ι) :
    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i) :=
  huniv i

variable (C π) in
/-- **A mixed-parameter chart family is admissible input to the DAT-glue seam.**

`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` accepts it verbatim.  This is the statement that settles the
question `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack` and I-0660 both left implicit: the representability engine
never sees a chart parameter, so the forced calibration `b = n` is a *per-chart* condition and
carries no uniformity obligation.

Note what remains hypothetical here and is not weakened by this: `hf` (i.e. `IsChartUniv`, still
CERT-Σ-gated), local surjectivity (DAT-B B-6), and the *existence* of `rep i` at parameters other
than `g` — which is the question this observation hands to the divisor-representability lane. -/
def mixedParamRepresentableBy {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i))
    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V))] :
    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
  pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V) hf

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre

/-!
# THE PRODUCER: `IsChartDatumPlusFibre` for a class in the image of the sheafification unit

## What this file closes

`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre.lean` proves CHART-U(b) at a general test from a per-affine-piece
`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, and its header says plainly what it does not do:

> The hypothesis is a *per-affine-piece existence of a datum with the plus-class property*, and
> nothing here produces such a datum.

**This file produces one**, and the ingredient that was missing is smaller than four successive
sessions on this leaf priced it: on an **affine** test the canonical field point `Over.testPoint t`
**is** the base-change morphism `overSpecMap A κ(t)`.  Both sides are `Spec` of the same ring map —
`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine` is *defined* as `Spec.preimage` of `fromSpecResidueField`,
so `Spec.map_preimage` closes it — but nothing in the tree said so, and every plus-class identity
on this lane is an identity between a class pulled along `Over.testPoint` and one pulled along
`relCurveMap`.  Without the comparison the two sides are not even syntactically comparable; with
it they are the same class.

## The shape of the producer, and its one genuine restriction

`IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D` compares `μ`'s fibre at `κ(t)`, read as a plus class, with the
plus-*unit* of `D`'s fibre class.  So the natural hypothesis on `μ` is that it is *already* a
plus unit — i.e. in the image of the sheafification unit `relPicToPicEt` — and then `D` comes
from `exists_cechPicClass_eq` applied to any Čech representative.

That restriction is real and is named `IsPlusHonest` below.  It is **not** vacuous and **not**
automatic:

* not automatic — a general plus class over `Spec A` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E`,
  and `Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean` is precisely the record that it becomes honest only over
  `E.Carrier`, not over `A`.  So `IsPlusHonest` is a genuine hypothesis, not a restatement;
* not vacuous, and this is the payoff — the range of `relPicToPicEt` is a **subgroup**, and every
  class the chart layer twists by is in it: the θ-family (`thetaFamily_isPlusHonest`), the
  Σ-family, and the Abel value itself (`abelDiv_isPlusHonest`).  So `chartTwist` preserves
  honesty, and CHART-U(b) becomes **unconditional** on exactly the classes DAT-C's Σ-chart reads.

  **A CORRECTION TO THIS PARAGRAPH, from a fresh-context review of the commit that first wrote
  it, and it is the same failure this leaf recorded one round earlier.**  When first committed the
  sentence above cited `abelDiv_isPlusHonest` **and that declaration did not exist** — a
  workspace-wide grep returned exactly one hit, the sentence itself.  That is precisely the
  failure mode r7 diagnosed (`docstring-declaration-lists-unchecked`) and filed a lesson about,
  reproduced by the very session that filed it, inside its own *non-vacuity* argument.
  A kernel check, a `sorry` census and an axiom probe are all silent about it.

  It also mattered mathematically, which is why it was worth writing rather than deleting: the
  θ- and Σ-witnesses are the **twist factors**, which `chartTwist_isPlusHonest` discharges anyway,
  so they say nothing about the class being *charted*.  Since `chartValue = abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹`,
  honesty of a chart value reduces to honesty of `abelDiv` alone — so `abelDiv_isPlusHonest` was
  carrying the whole of the final clause.  It is now proved (below), so the paragraph stands as
  written; had it not been, the honest statement would have been "no residue beyond
  `IsPlusHonest lam`", with the Σ-chart clause unproved.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.testPoint_eq_overSpecMap` — **the comparison**: on an affine test the
  canonical field point is the base-change morphism.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt` — the producer, with the datum given.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range` — **the producer proper**: for a
  class in the image of the unit, a datum with the plus-class property EXISTS.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsPlusHonest` — the per-affine-piece form, closed under the group operations.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest` — **CHART-U(b) with no residue** for an
  honest class, and `chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest` the same open as DATA.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161). -/
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
open TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open AlgebraicJacobian

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-! ## The comparison: on an affine test the field point IS the base change -/

/-- **On an affine test, the canonical field point is the base-change morphism.**

`Over.testPoint t : overSpec k κ(t) ⟶ overSpec k A` is built from mathlib's
`Scheme.fromSpecResidueField`, while `overSpecMap A κ(t)` is `Spec` of `algebraMap A κ(t)`.  They
are equal because the `A`-algebra structure on `κ(t)` (`instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`) is
*defined* to be `Spec.preimage` of that very morphism, so `Spec.map_preimage` is the whole proof.

**Why this was the gate.**  Every plus-class identity on this lane compares a class pulled along
`Over.testPoint` (the `chartLocus` side, indexed by points of a test) with one pulled along
`relCurveMap C A κ(t)` (the datum side, indexed by base change).  Absent this lemma the two are
not syntactically comparable and no producer can be written; with it they are the same morphism
and the producer below is three rewrites.  The lemma is *cheap*, which is the point: four
sessions on this leaf priced the missing producer as the identification of a fibre class, i.e.
as geometry, when what was missing was a comparison of two spellings of one morphism. -/
theorem testPoint_eq_overSpecMap {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
    Over.testPoint t
      = overSpecMap (k := k) A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) := by
  apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
  simp only [Over.testPoint_left, overSpecMap_left]
  rw [Over.algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine]

rw [Over.algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine]
  exact (Spec.map_preimage _).symm

omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
  [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
/-- The whiskered form: the relative-curve comparison at the field point of an affine test is
`relCurveMap`.  This is the shape `IsChartDatumPlusFibre` reads on its right-hand side. -/
theorem relCurveMap_testPoint {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
    (C ◁ Over.testPoint t).left
      = relCurveMap C A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) := by
  rw [testPoint_eq_overSpecMap]
  rfl

/-! ## The producer -/

omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
variable (C π) in
/-- **THE PRODUCER, with the datum supplied**: if `μ` is the unit image of a relative Picard
class presented by the Čech class `L₀`, then any datum whose class is `L₀` satisfies
`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`.

The proof is four rewrites and no geometry.  `picEtMap_relPicToPicEt` moves the restriction to
`κ(t)` inside the unit; `picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt` collapses the affine comparison to
`PicEtAff.unit`; `PicEtAff.map_id` deletes the identity restriction `κ(t) → κ(t)` that
`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`'s left-hand side carries; and `relCurveMap_testPoint` identifies
the two spellings of the base change.

Note which hypotheses are absent: no witness, no `H¹`, no divisor, no degree, no separability,
and no certificate.  The plus-class identity was never geometry — it is the statement that the
two ways of restricting a *unit* to a residue field agree.

**A measurement, not a claim, and it is independent evidence for that reading**: this theorem does
not use `GeometricallyReduced C.hom` either — the linter says so, hence the `omit`.  A statement
about a fibre class would need the curve's geometry; this one needs the curve only to have the
functor defined. -/
theorem isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (L₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k A).left.CechPic) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π)
    (hD : D.cechPicClass = L₀) :
    IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π
      (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k A) (relPicMk C (overSpec k A) L₀)) D := by
  intro t
  rw [picEtMap_relPicToPicEt, picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt, PicEtAff.map_id, hD,
    relPicMap_mk, relCurveMap_testPoint]
  rfl

omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
variable (C π) in
/-- **THE PRODUCER PROPER**: for a class in the image of the sheafification unit, a datum with
the plus-class property EXISTS.

The datum comes from `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq` (the extraction keystone,
`Cohomology/GluedSheafExtraction.lean:301`) applied to any Čech representative of the class, and
`relPicMk_surjective` supplies the representative.  So the existential
`isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre` asks for is met outright, with no choice left to the caller.

This is the statement `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre.lean`'s header names as not claimed, and it
too is `GeometricallyReduced`-free. -/
theorem exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A))
    (hμ : ∃ z : relPic C (overSpec k A), relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k A) z = μ) :
    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π, IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D := by
  obtain ⟨z, rfl⟩ := hμ
  obtain ⟨L₀, rfl⟩ := relPicMk_surjective C (overSpec k A) z
  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq
    (C := C) (B := A) (π := π) L₀
  exact ⟨D, isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt C π L₀ D hD⟩

/-! ## The honesty hypothesis, and why it is not vacuous -/

variable (C) in
/-- **The honesty hypothesis: `μ` is a plus unit on every affine piece of the test.**

This is the one thing the producer needs of `μ`, and it is a genuine hypothesis rather than a
restatement: a plus class over `Spec A` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E`, and
`Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean` is the record that it becomes honest over `E.Carrier` and not over
`A`.  So `IsPlusHonest` is exactly the gap between an arbitrary class and one the producer reaches.

It is stated per affine piece because that is the shape `isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre` consumes;
over an affine test it is the single condition that `μ` is in the range of `relPicToPicEt`. -/
def IsPlusHonest (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (μ : picEt C T) : Prop :=
  ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens, ∃ z : relPic C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)),
    relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)) z
      = picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) μ

omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] in
variable (C) in
/-- Honesty is closed under multiplication — the range of `relPicToPicEt` is a subgroup, and
`picEtMap` is a homomorphism. -/
theorem IsPlusHonest.mul {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {μ ν : picEt C T}
    (hμ : IsPlusHonest C T μ) (hν : IsPlusHonest C T ν) :
    IsPlusHonest C T (μ * ν) := by
  intro U
  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hμ U
  obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := hν U
  exact ⟨z * w, by rw [map_mul, hz, hw, map_mul]⟩

omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] in
variable (C) in
/-- Honesty is closed under inversion. -/
theorem IsPlusHonest.inv {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {μ : picEt C T}
    (hμ : IsPlusHonest C T μ) :
    IsPlusHonest C T μ⁻¹ := by
  intro U
  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hμ U
  exact ⟨z⁻¹, by rw [map_inv, hz, map_inv]⟩

omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] in
variable (C) in
/-- Honesty is closed under powers. -/
theorem IsPlusHonest.pow {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {μ : picEt C T}
    (hμ : IsPlusHonest C T μ) (m : ℕ) :
    IsPlusHonest C T (μ ^ m) := by
  intro U
  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hμ U
  exact ⟨z ^ m, by rw [map_pow, hz, map_pow]⟩

variable (C) in
/-- **A θ-family is honest at every test** — the first half of the non-vacuity check.

`thetaFamily_natural` restricts a θ-family to a θ-family, and `thetaFamily_overSpec_affineEquiv`
says its affine collapse is the plus unit of the base-changed base class.  So a θ-family is in the
range of the unit on every affine piece, with no hypothesis on the curve.

This is why `chartTwist` preserves honesty: two of its three factors are θ-families. -/
theorem thetaFamily_isPlusHonest (L₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic)
    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    IsPlusHonest C T (thetaFamily C L₀ T) := by
  intro U
  refine ⟨relPicAlgMap C (Algebra.ofId k Γ(T.left, U.1)) (relPicMk C (overSpec k k) L₀), ?_⟩
  rw [thetaFamily_natural]
  exact (picEtAffineEquiv C Γ(T.left, U.1)).injective (by
    rw [picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt, thetaFamily_overSpec_affineEquiv])

variable (C) in
/-- A Σ-family is honest: it *is* a θ-family (`sigmaFamily` is defined as one). -/
theorem sigmaFamily_isPlusHonest (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    IsPlusHonest C T (sigmaFamily C Z T) :=
  thetaFamily_isPlusHonest C _ T

variable (C π) in
/-- **THE ABEL VALUE IS HONEST AT EVERY TEST** — the witness that carries weight, and the one this
file's header cited by name before it existed (see the header's own retraction).

The θ- and Σ-family witnesses above are the *twist factors*, which `chartTwist_isPlusHonest`
discharges anyway; they say nothing about the class being charted.  Since
`chartValue = abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹` and honesty is a subgroup condition, honesty of a **chart
value** reduces to honesty of `abelDiv` — so this is the row that makes CHART-U(b) unconditional
on the classes DAT-C's Σ-chart actually reads.

It is cheap for a structural reason: `abelDiv`'s components are `abelDivPlus`, i.e. `PicEtAff.unit`
of `relPicMk` of the family's class, and `relPicToPicEt`'s components are `PicEtAff.unit` of
`relPicMap` — so the witness on the piece `U` is the class of the *restricted* family, and
`abelDiv_val` plus `picEtMap_abelDiv` line the two up. -/
theorem abelDiv_isPlusHonest {n : ℕ} (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (s : divFamZar C π n T) :
    IsPlusHonest C T (abelDiv C π n T s) := by
  intro U
  refine ⟨relPicMk C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1))
    ((divFamZarAffineEquiv C π n Γ(T.left, U.1)
      (divFamZar.map C π n (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) s)).picClass), ?_⟩
  rw [picEtMap_abelDiv, abelDiv_overSpec]
  rfl

variable (C) in
/-- **`chartTwist` PRESERVES honesty** — the reason the producer reaches the Σ-chart.

`chartTwist λ = λ · θᵐ · Σ⁻¹`, and both twist factors are θ-families, hence honest at every test
with no hypothesis.  Since honesty is a subgroup condition, the twisted class is honest exactly
when `λ` is.

So the residue of CHART-U(b) is **the λ-factor alone**: no twist bookkeeping enters, which is the
mis-pricing the §3.3 correction 5 records. -/
theorem chartTwist_isPlusHonest (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) {lam : picEt C T} (hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam) :
    IsPlusHonest C T (chartTwist C m Z T lam) := by
  rw [chartTwist]
  exact (hlam.mul C ((thetaFamily_isPlusHonest C (thetaCechClass C) T).pow C m)).mul C
    ((sigmaFamily_isPlusHonest C Z T).inv C)

/-! ## CHART-U(b) with the residue discharged -/

set_option linter.overlappingInstances false in
variable (C π) in
/-- **CHART-U(b) AT A GENERAL TEST, WITH NO RESIDUE**, for a class that is honest on the affine
pieces of the test.

`isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre` needs a per-piece datum with the plus-class property;
`exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range` produces one from honesty, and
`chartTwist_isPlusHonest` says the twist does not disturb honesty.  So the whole chain — the
engine, RE-5, the dictionary, the fibre-field invariance, `haff`, the presentation, `hconv`,
`hplus`, and now the producer — closes on the single hypothesis `IsPlusHonest`.

`IsAffineHom π` follows from `IsFinite π`, whence the disabled overlapping-instance linter — the
same configuration `chartLocusAffineLocal_of_plusFibre` carries and for the same reason. -/
theorem isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) (hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam) :
    IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z lam) :=
  isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre C π hπ m Z T lam fun U =>
    exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range C π _
      (by
        obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := chartTwist_isPlusHonest C m Z T hlam U
        exact ⟨z, hz.trans (picEtMap_chartTwist m Z (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam)⟩)

set_option linter.overlappingInstances false in
variable (C π) in
/-- **The chart locus as an OPEN OF THE TEST, from honesty alone** — the shape the `W` field of a
chart datum consumes (`chartLocusOpens`, `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:115`), with its `haff`
argument discharged rather than passed through.

This is c9b's clause (i) paid in full for an honest class: not "reduced to", but produced. -/
def chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) (hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam) :
    T.left.Opens where
  carrier := chartLocus C m Z lam
  is_open' := isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest C π hπ m Z T lam hlam

@[simp]
lemma mem_chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest
    {hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom}
    {m : ℕ} {Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor}
    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} {hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam}
    {t : T.left} :
    t ∈ chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest C π hπ m Z T lam hlam ↔ t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam :=
  Iff.rfl

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

10	# COVERAGE NEEDS NO DROP, NO ORACLE, AND NO STEP 6
11	
12	A retraction of this lane's own account of B-5, and it removes a residue rather than adding one.
13	
14	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageTest.lean`'s DEFECT section establishes — correctly — that the
15	`w4-datb` §1.2 argument as written runs the greedy drop at `Z := 0` and feeds the drop's
16	**output** `Σ` back as the chart index's `Z`, so that the two stages carry different `Z`, and
17	that this feedback ("step 6") is not discharged anywhere.  It records step 6 as one of B-5's
18	open residues.
19	
20	**Step 6 is not a residue, because coverage does not need the drop at all.**
21	
22	## Why: read what `chartLocus` actually asks for
23	
24	`IsSplitWitness` (`Pic0ChartLocus.lean:151`) — and its own docstring says this at length, under
25	"A convention this predicate INHERITS" — asks for a divisor `W` in the presenting class with
26	`Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))`, and asks for **neither `0 ≤ W` nor `deg W = g`**.  Effectivity and the
27	degree normalisation are what the *chart map's injectivity* needs (GAP-2, `h⁰ = 1`), not what
28	*membership of the locus* needs.
29	
30	The drop (`RiemannRoch/CoverageDrop.lean`) exists to manufacture exactly those two extra
31	properties: it takes a degree-`g+e` witness with `h¹ = 0` and produces an effective `S` with
32	`h⁰(W₀ − S) = 1`.  For membership, that work is thrown away — `mem_chartLocus_of_drop` returns
33	the `IsSplitWitness` half from `hW₀`/`h1` alone, and its own proof shows this: the split witness
34	comes from `isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C μ m Z M₀ hM₀ W₀ hW₀ h1`, in which the drop,
35	the oracle `P`, `hdense`, `hPcl`, `hPdeg`, `g`, `e`, `hχ` and `hdeg` **do not appear**.
36	
37	So the feedback of step 6 was an artefact of routing coverage through the drop.  Cut the drop
38	and there is one `Z` again — the chart index's — and nothing to feed back.
39	
40	## What coverage then needs, in full
41	
42	Exactly one input beyond the landed splitting: a divisor of the twisted fibre class over the
43	splitting field with vanishing `H¹`.  That is DAT-0a at the fibre field, and it is genuinely
44	per-fibre (I-0204, `w4-datb` §0.2.2): no uniform `m₀` exists, so the exponent `m` must be chosen

51	`n` the `hdeg` hypothesis **forces `b = n`**, and at `n = g` the resulting `hb` is a statement

53	`mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` itself and `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` for the

8	/-!
9	# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
12	is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
13	of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
14	verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
15	index per point of `T`".
16	
17	**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
18	produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
19	chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
20	membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
21	`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
22	connection is what this file supplies.
23	
24	## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
25	
26	Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:
27	
28	* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
29	  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
30	  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
31	  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
32	* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
33	  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
34	  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
35	  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
36	* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
37	  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
38	  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
39	  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.
40	
41	## Main declarations
42	
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
44	  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
45	  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
47	  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
48	  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise` — the composite: pointwise
50	  coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, i.e.
51	  B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the **converse**, and the reason this
53	  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
54	  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
55	  strengthening chosen to be provable.
56	-/

66	
67	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}

69	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
70	
71	noncomputable section
72	
73	/-! ## The bridge, with no chart content
74	
75	Stated for an arbitrary family of sieves on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses:
76	the coverage half of B-5 is a statement about the *site*, and mixing it with the presheaf
77	statement is what made it look gated. -/
78	
79	/-- **Pointwise data gives a covering supremum sieve.**
80	
81	If every point `t` of `T` has an open neighbourhood `W t` and an index `idx t` such that the
82	inclusion `(W t).ι` lies in the `idx t`-th sieve, then the supremum of the family is a
83	Zariski covering sieve of `T`.
84	
85	The proof is the cover `{W t}_{t : ↥T}` — jointly surjective because `t ∈ W t`, open
86	immersions because they are opens inclusions — fed to `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`, and
87	then `le_iSup` at the index of the destructed point.
88	
89	Note there is **no compatibility condition between different points**: `idx` is an arbitrary
90	function.  That is why chart-parameter heterogeneity (dat-b row, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`)
91	costs nothing here — a supremum sieve never asks its members to agree. -/
92	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {T : Scheme.{u}}
93	    (Sv : ι → Sieve T) (W : ↥T → T.Opens) (hW : ∀ t, t ∈ W t) (idx : ↥T → ι)
94	    (hmem : ∀ t, (Sv (idx t)).arrows (W t).ι) :
95	    (⨆ i, Sv i) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
96	  refine Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
97	    ⟨Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers (↥T) (fun t => (W t : Scheme.{u})) (fun t => (W t).ι)
98	      (fun t => ⟨t, ⟨t, hW t⟩, rfl⟩) (fun t => inferInstance), ?_⟩
99	  rintro V g ⟨t⟩
100	  exact le_iSup Sv (idx t) _ (hmem t)
101	
102	/-! ## `ChartsCoverLocally` from what B-5 actually produces -/
103	
104	variable (C) in
105	/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.
106	
107	The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
108	field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
109	it, and every point `t` of `T`:
110	
111	* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
112	  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
113	  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
114	* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
115	  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
116	* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
117	  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
118	* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.
119	
120	Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
121	a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
122	four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.
123	
124	**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
125	and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
126	It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
127	written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
128	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
129	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
130	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
131	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
132	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
133	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
134	  intro T s
135	  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
136	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩
137	
138	variable (C) in
139	/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.
140	
141	The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
142	Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
143	remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
144	instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
145	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
146	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
147	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
148	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
149	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
150	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
151	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)
152	
153	/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening
154	
155	A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
156	disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
157	the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/
158	
159	variable (C) in
160	/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**
161	
162	The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
163	From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
164	and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.
165	
166	**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
167	an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
168	open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
169	(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
170	the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
171	pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
172	exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
173	theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
174	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
175	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (T : Scheme.{u})
176	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
177	    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
178	      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
179	        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
180	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
181	  refine ⟨𝒰, fun j => ?_⟩
182	  have hj := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
183	  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hj
184	  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hj
185	  exact ⟨i, x, hx⟩
186	
187	end
188	
189	end AlgebraicGeometry

16	[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]

19	which is dat-b row B-6.  Three files carry that instance as a `variable`
20	(`JacobianDataCharts.lean:117`, `JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean:183`,
21	`JacobianDataAbelImage.lean:131`) and **nothing anywhere produces one**.  This file supplies
22	the producer, in the form that DAT-B's coverage statement can actually feed.
23	
24	## What local surjectivity unfolds to, and why that matters here
25	
26	Mathlib's `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J f` has a single field: for every object `T` and
27	every section `s` of the target at `T`, the *image sieve* of `s` — the sieve of maps
28	`g : T' ⟶ T` along which `s` pulls back into the image of `f` — is a covering sieve.
29	
30	For the Zariski topology on schemes that is exactly the geometric statement dat-b row B-5
31	proves: **every degree-zero class on a test is, locally on that test, a chart value**.  So
32	B-6 is not a further geometric obligation on top of B-5 — it is B-5 phrased against
33	mathlib's sieve-theoretic interface, plus the bookkeeping that turns a family of charts into
34	`Sigma.desc`.
35	
36	The bookkeeping is what this file provides, and it is not trivial: the section must be hit
37	by *some* chart of the family, and `Sigma.desc` must be shown to see it.  That is
38	`ChartsCoverLocally` below.
39	
40	## The honest scope, stated up front
41	
42	`ChartsCoverLocally` is the hypothesis, not a theorem.  Its content is B-5 and B-5's residue
43	is recorded on the dat-b roadmap row (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation).  What
44	this file establishes is that **nothing else** stands between B-5 and the instance the
45	producer needs — in particular no compatibility across charts, because `Sigma.desc` has
46	none to check.
47	
48	## Main declarations
49	
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartsCoverLocally` — the coverage hypothesis, stated exactly as the
51	  image sieve of `Sigma.desc` being covering, but spelled in terms of the individual charts
52	  so a producer never has to reason about the coproduct.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` — **B-6**: that hypothesis gives the
54	  instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_forall_surjective` — the degenerate sufficient
56	  condition (a chart that is surjective on points of every test already covers), recorded so
57	  the hypothesis is visibly *satisfiable* and not a disguised falsehood.
58	-/

102	exactly the same footing as a homogeneous one. -/
103	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
104	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
105	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) :
106	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) where
107	  imageSieve_mem {T} s := by
108	    refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.superset_covering ?_ (h T s)
109	    refine iSup_le fun i => ?_
110	    rintro T' g ⟨t, ht⟩
111	    -- transport the witness along `Sigma.ι` and use `Sigma.ι_desc`
112	    refine ⟨(Sigma.ι (fun j => yoneda.obj (X j)) i).app (op T') t, ?_⟩
113	    rw [← ht, ← NatTrans.comp_app_apply, Sigma.ι_desc f i]
114	
115	/-- **The hypothesis is satisfiable, checked rather than assumed.**
116	
117	If one chart of the family is surjective on the points of every test, the coverage hypothesis
118	holds — its image sieve is already the maximal sieve.  This is the degenerate case (and not
119	the geometric situation: no single Abel chart is surjective on all tests), but it rules out
120	the failure mode where a `Prop`-valued hypothesis turns out to be unsatisfiable and the
121	"reduction" above is therefore vacuous.
122	
123	Compare the two-sided check in `Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`: there the question was whether the
124	datum was too *weak*; here it is whether it is too *strong*. -/
125	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_forall_surjective {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
126	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (i : ι)
127	    (hi : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ, Function.Surjective ((f i).app T)) :
128	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
129	  intro T s
130	  refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.superset_covering ?_
131	    (Scheme.zariskiTopology.top_mem T)
132	  intro T' g _
133	  exact le_iSup (fun j => Presheaf.imageSieve (f j) s) i g (hi (op T') _)
134	
135	end
136	
137	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise
7	
8	/-!
9	# B-5 at the Abel chart: what the pointwise datum unfolds to, and what it costs
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` reduces `ChartsCoverLocally` — hence B-6 — to a
12	four-part datum at each point of each test.  That reduction is stated for an *arbitrary*
13	family of presheaf maps, so it says nothing about how hard the datum is at the family that
14	matters.  This file instantiates it at `abelSigmaChart` and computes the answer.
15	
16	## The computation, and the one thing it makes visible
17	
18	A section of `pic0SigmaSheaf C` over a **bare** test scheme `T` is by definition a *pair*
19	`⟨a, λ⟩` with `a : T ⟶ Spec k` and `λ` a degree-zero class on the slice object `Over.mk a`
20	(`Over.sigmaExtension`, `Picard/OverSigmaExtension.lean`).  And `(Over.mk a).left` is `T`
21	itself, definitionally.  So the big-site/slice crossing that looks like it needs a bridge does
22	not: the pointwise datum's `t : ↥T` *is* a point of the slice test, and `chartLocus` applies to
23	it with no transport.  `abelChartApp_eq` below records the crossing as an equation rather than
24	leaving it to unfold at a use site.
25	
26	What the computation *does* make visible is where the cost sits.  `abelSigmaChart`'s value at
27	`x : W ⟶ D.left` is `⟨x ≫ D.hom, chartValue … (rep.homEquiv …)⟩`, so matching it against the
28	restriction of `⟨a, λ⟩` needs **both** components: the Σ-component is an equation between
29	morphisms to `Spec k`, and only then is there a class equation.  A producer that supplies the
30	class half alone has not supplied the datum — the Σ-component is what pins the chart point to
31	lie *over* the test, and it is free only because `W.ι ≫ a` is what `D.hom` must equal.
32	
33	## THE CORRECTION THIS FILE CARRIES, against this lane's own headline
34	
35	`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:40` says of its `chartLocusOpens`:
36	
37	> `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised — the `W` field costs zero, which is
38	> a real reduction of the datum from four fields to three
39	
40	**The second clause is false, and the roadmap `c9b` row repeats it** ("`W` needs nothing").
41	`chartLocusOpens` takes an argument `haff`, the affine-local openness of the locus at every
42	affine open of the test, and *nothing in the tree discharges it*:
43	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsoInvariance.lean`) removed the
44	`IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` hypothesis and passes `haff` straight through, as does
45	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` before it.  The affine case that would feed it is
46	`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`), which is
47	itself conditional on `IsChartDatumPresentation` — B-4's *named residue*.
48	
49	**Update, same session** (`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationConverse.lean`): that residue is now
50	*entirely witness-free*.  Its forward half already was (the trivial splitting), and its
51	converse `hconv` — the descent direction, open for three sessions — is discharged by plus-unit
52	injectivity.  So what `haff` ultimately costs is a `cechPicClass` base-change identity: no
53	witness, no `H¹`, no divisor, and nothing certificate- or divRep-gated.
54	
55	So the honest accounting is: **`W` costs `haff`, which costs B-4's presentation residue.**  The
56	datum went from four fields to three *shapes* but not to three *obligations*.  What is
57	genuinely free is the type-level crossing above, and `chartLocusHaff` below is the residue
58	named so it cannot be lost again.
59	
60	## Main declarations
61	
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelChartApp_eq` — the Abel chart's value at a point of the divisor
63	  scheme, as an explicit `Sigma.mk`.  Both components, since the datum needs both.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartLocusAffineLocal` — the `haff` residue, named.  This is what
65	  `chartLocusOpens` silently costs.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusOpens_of_affineLocal` — `chartLocusOpens` from it, so the
67	  dependency is explicit in the API rather than in an argument position.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation` — the residue **reduced to B-4's
69	  own named obligation**: a per-affine-piece `IsChartDatumPresentation` gives it.  This is the
70	  link that was asserted in `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring and never written.
71	-/
72	
73	set_option autoImplicit false
74	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
75	
76	universe u
77	
78	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
79	
80	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
81	
82	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
83	
84	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
85	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
86	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
87	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
88	
89	noncomputable section
90	
91	/-! ## The Abel chart's value, both components -/
92	
93	/-- **The Abel chart map evaluated at a point of the divisor scheme.**
94	
95	`abelSigmaChart` is `rep.toSigmaExtension ≫ Over.sigmaExtensionNat (chartValueTrans …)`, and
96	both factors act componentwise on the Σ-extension, so the value at `x : Y ⟶ D.left` is the
97	pair whose structure morphism is `x ≫ D.hom` and whose class is the chart value of the divisor
98	family `rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl)`.
99	
100	Recorded as an equation because a coverage producer has to match this against a *given*
101	section, and the match is two equations rather than one: the Σ-components must agree before
102	the classes are even in the same type.  Leaving it to unfold at the use site is how the
103	Σ-component gets forgotten. -/
104	@[simp]
105	theorem abelChartApp_eq {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
106	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
107	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
108	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
109	    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (x : Y ⟶ D.left) :
110	    (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg).app (op Y) x
111	      = ⟨x ≫ D.hom, ⟨chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x ≫ D.hom))
112	          (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl)),
113	        chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg _ _⟩⟩ :=
114	  rfl
115	
116	/-! ## The `haff` residue, named
117	
118	`chartLocusOpens` takes the affine-local openness as an argument.  Naming it is not cosmetic:
119	an argument in a definition's signature is invisible to a census of open obligations, which is
120	how "the `W` field costs zero" survived into two roadmap rows. -/
121	
122	variable (C) in
123	/-- **The affine-local openness residue of `chartLocus`** — what `chartLocusOpens` costs.
124	
125	For a test `T` and a class `lam` on it, this says the chart locus is open over every affine
126	open piece of `T`.  It is exactly the `haff` argument of `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'`,
127	and it is the *only* remaining input to CHART-U(b) at a general test: the iso-invariance
128	hypothesis that used to sit beside it was discharged
129	(`isSplitWitnessIsoInvariant_holds`), but this one was passed through, not proved.
130	
131	Named as a `Prop` so that it appears in searches for open obligations. -/
132	def ChartLocusAffineLocal (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
133	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) : Prop :=
134	  ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
135	    IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))
136	
137	variable (C) in
138	/-- `chartLocusOpens` with its cost made explicit in the API.
139	
140	Identical in content to `chartLocusOpens` — the point is that the dependency is now a named
141	`Prop` a reader can grep for, rather than an unnamed argument that reads as bookkeeping. -/
142	def chartLocusOpens' (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
143	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
144	    (haff : ChartLocusAffineLocal C m Z T lam) : T.left.Opens :=
145	  chartLocusOpens C m Z T lam haff
146	
147	@[simp]
148	lemma mem_chartLocusOpens' {m : ℕ} {Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor}
149	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} {haff : ChartLocusAffineLocal C m Z T lam}
150	    {t : T.left} :
151	    t ∈ chartLocusOpens' C m Z T lam haff ↔ t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam :=
152	  Iff.rfl
153	
154	/-! ## Reducing the residue to B-4's own named obligation
155	
156	`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`'s docstring says the general-test statement follows from the
157	affine one "by the affine-piece locality of the (b-amendment)'s transport (iii)", and adds that
158	it "is not stated here only because it would need the presentation hypothesis *per affine
159	piece*".  That is right, and this is the statement it describes. -/
160	
161	set_option linter.overlappingInstances false in
162	variable (C π) in
163	/-- **The `haff` residue from a per-affine-piece presentation** — the link
164	`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring describes and does not state.
165	
166	For each affine open `U` of the test, a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `Γ(T.left, U)` presenting
167	the restricted twisted class gives openness of the locus on that piece
168	(`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation`), and `chartLocus` over the piece *is* that set
169	by definition (`chartLocus` unfolds to the split-witness set of the twisted class, and the
170	twist commutes with restriction by `picEtMap_chartTwist`).
171	
172	So the affine-local residue is **exactly** B-4's presentation obligation, quantified over
173	affine pieces — no extra geometry, and in particular nothing certificate- or divRep-gated.
174	Combined with `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` this closes CHART-U(b) at a general test the
175	moment `IsChartDatumPresentation` is available per piece.
176	
177	The `hπ` and `IsFinite π` hypotheses are the ones
178	`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` carries.  `IsFinite π` is strictly stronger than
179	the file-level `IsAffineHom π` (whence the overlapping-instance warning, disabled below): the
180	affine openness route runs through the rigid engine, which needs finiteness, while the rest of
181	this file needs only affineness. -/
182	theorem chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation [IsFinite π]
183	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
184	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
185	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
186	    (hpres : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
187	      ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C (Γ(T.left, U.1)) π,
188	        IsChartDatumPresentation C π
189	          (chartTwist C m Z _ (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam)) D) :
190	    ChartLocusAffineLocal C m Z T lam := by
191	  intro U
192	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := hpres U
193	  exact isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation C π hπ hD
194	
195	end
196	
197	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre
7	
8	/-!
9	# THE PRODUCER: `IsChartDatumPlusFibre` for a class in the image of the sheafification unit
10	
11	## What this file closes
12	
13	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre.lean` proves CHART-U(b) at a general test from a per-affine-piece
14	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, and its header says plainly what it does not do:
15	
16	> The hypothesis is a *per-affine-piece existence of a datum with the plus-class property*, and
17	> nothing here produces such a datum.
18	
19	**This file produces one**, and the ingredient that was missing is smaller than four successive
20	sessions on this leaf priced it: on an **affine** test the canonical field point `Over.testPoint t`
21	**is** the base-change morphism `overSpecMap A κ(t)`.  Both sides are `Spec` of the same ring map —
22	`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine` is *defined* as `Spec.preimage` of `fromSpecResidueField`,
23	so `Spec.map_preimage` closes it — but nothing in the tree said so, and every plus-class identity
24	on this lane is an identity between a class pulled along `Over.testPoint` and one pulled along
25	`relCurveMap`.  Without the comparison the two sides are not even syntactically comparable; with
26	it they are the same class.
27	
28	## The shape of the producer, and its one genuine restriction
29	
30	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D` compares `μ`'s fibre at `κ(t)`, read as a plus class, with the
31	plus-*unit* of `D`'s fibre class.  So the natural hypothesis on `μ` is that it is *already* a
32	plus unit — i.e. in the image of the sheafification unit `relPicToPicEt` — and then `D` comes
33	from `exists_cechPicClass_eq` applied to any Čech representative.
34	
35	That restriction is real and is named `IsPlusHonest` below.  It is **not** vacuous and **not**
36	automatic:
37	
38	* not automatic — a general plus class over `Spec A` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E`,
39	  and `Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean` is precisely the record that it becomes honest only over
40	  `E.Carrier`, not over `A`.  So `IsPlusHonest` is a genuine hypothesis, not a restatement;
41	* not vacuous, and this is the payoff — the range of `relPicToPicEt` is a **subgroup**, and every
42	  class the chart layer twists by is in it: the θ-family (`thetaFamily_isPlusHonest`), the
43	  Σ-family, and the Abel value itself (`abelDiv_isPlusHonest`).  So `chartTwist` preserves
44	  honesty, and CHART-U(b) becomes **unconditional** on exactly the classes DAT-C's Σ-chart reads.
45	
46	  **A CORRECTION TO THIS PARAGRAPH, from a fresh-context review of the commit that first wrote
47	  it, and it is the same failure this leaf recorded one round earlier.**  When first committed the
48	  sentence above cited `abelDiv_isPlusHonest` **and that declaration did not exist** — a
49	  workspace-wide grep returned exactly one hit, the sentence itself.  That is precisely the
50	  failure mode r7 diagnosed (`docstring-declaration-lists-unchecked`) and filed a lesson about,
51	  reproduced by the very session that filed it, inside its own *non-vacuity* argument.
52	  A kernel check, a `sorry` census and an axiom probe are all silent about it.
53	
54	  It also mattered mathematically, which is why it was worth writing rather than deleting: the
55	  θ- and Σ-witnesses are the **twist factors**, which `chartTwist_isPlusHonest` discharges anyway,
56	  so they say nothing about the class being *charted*.  Since `chartValue = abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹`,
57	  honesty of a chart value reduces to honesty of `abelDiv` alone — so `abelDiv_isPlusHonest` was
58	  carrying the whole of the final clause.  It is now proved (below), so the paragraph stands as
59	  written; had it not been, the honest statement would have been "no residue beyond
60	  `IsPlusHonest lam`", with the Σ-chart clause unproved.
61	
62	## Main declarations
63	
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.testPoint_eq_overSpecMap` — **the comparison**: on an affine test the
65	  canonical field point is the base-change morphism.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt` — the producer, with the datum given.
67	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range` — **the producer proper**: for a
68	  class in the image of the unit, a datum with the plus-class property EXISTS.
69	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsPlusHonest` — the per-affine-piece form, closed under the group operations.
70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest` — **CHART-U(b) with no residue** for an
71	  honest class, and `chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest` the same open as DATA.
72	-/
73	
74	set_option autoImplicit false
75	/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/
76	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
77	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161). -/
78	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
79	
80	universe u
81	
82	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
83	open TopologicalSpace Opposite
84	
85	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
86	
87	open AlgebraicJacobian
88	
89	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
90	
91	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
92	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
93	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
94	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
95	
96	noncomputable section
97	
98	/-! ## The comparison: on an affine test the field point IS the base change -/
99	
100	/-- **On an affine test, the canonical field point is the base-change morphism.**
101	
102	`Over.testPoint t : overSpec k κ(t) ⟶ overSpec k A` is built from mathlib's
103	`Scheme.fromSpecResidueField`, while `overSpecMap A κ(t)` is `Spec` of `algebraMap A κ(t)`.  They
104	are equal because the `A`-algebra structure on `κ(t)` (`instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`) is
105	*defined* to be `Spec.preimage` of that very morphism, so `Spec.map_preimage` is the whole proof.
106	
107	**Why this was the gate.**  Every plus-class identity on this lane compares a class pulled along
108	`Over.testPoint` (the `chartLocus` side, indexed by points of a test) with one pulled along
109	`relCurveMap C A κ(t)` (the datum side, indexed by base change).  Absent this lemma the two are
110	not syntactically comparable and no producer can be written; with it they are the same morphism
111	and the producer below is three rewrites.  The lemma is *cheap*, which is the point: four
112	sessions on this leaf priced the missing producer as the identification of a fibre class, i.e.
113	as geometry, when what was missing was a comparison of two spellings of one morphism. -/
114	theorem testPoint_eq_overSpecMap {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
115	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
116	    Over.testPoint t
117	      = overSpecMap (k := k) A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) := by
118	  apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
119	  simp only [Over.testPoint_left, overSpecMap_left]
120	  rw [Over.algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine]
121	  exact (Spec.map_preimage _).symm
122	
123	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
124	  [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
125	/-- The whiskered form: the relative-curve comparison at the field point of an affine test is
126	`relCurveMap`.  This is the shape `IsChartDatumPlusFibre` reads on its right-hand side. -/
127	theorem relCurveMap_testPoint {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
128	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
129	    (C ◁ Over.testPoint t).left
130	      = relCurveMap C A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) := by
131	  rw [testPoint_eq_overSpecMap]
132	  rfl
133	
134	/-! ## The producer -/
135	
136	omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
137	variable (C π) in
138	/-- **THE PRODUCER, with the datum supplied**: if `μ` is the unit image of a relative Picard
139	class presented by the Čech class `L₀`, then any datum whose class is `L₀` satisfies
140	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`.
141	
142	The proof is four rewrites and no geometry.  `picEtMap_relPicToPicEt` moves the restriction to
143	`κ(t)` inside the unit; `picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt` collapses the affine comparison to
144	`PicEtAff.unit`; `PicEtAff.map_id` deletes the identity restriction `κ(t) → κ(t)` that
145	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`'s left-hand side carries; and `relCurveMap_testPoint` identifies
146	the two spellings of the base change.
147	
148	Note which hypotheses are absent: no witness, no `H¹`, no divisor, no degree, no separability,
149	and no certificate.  The plus-class identity was never geometry — it is the statement that the
150	two ways of restricting a *unit* to a residue field agree.
151	
152	**A measurement, not a claim, and it is independent evidence for that reading**: this theorem does
153	not use `GeometricallyReduced C.hom` either — the linter says so, hence the `omit`.  A statement
154	about a fibre class would need the curve's geometry; this one needs the curve only to have the
155	functor defined. -/
156	theorem isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
157	    (L₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k A).left.CechPic) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π)
158	    (hD : D.cechPicClass = L₀) :
159	    IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π
160	      (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k A) (relPicMk C (overSpec k A) L₀)) D := by
161	  intro t
162	  rw [picEtMap_relPicToPicEt, picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt, PicEtAff.map_id, hD,
163	    relPicMap_mk, relCurveMap_testPoint]
164	  rfl
165	
166	omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
167	variable (C π) in
168	/-- **THE PRODUCER PROPER**: for a class in the image of the sheafification unit, a datum with
169	the plus-class property EXISTS.
170	
171	The datum comes from `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq` (the extraction keystone,
172	`Cohomology/GluedSheafExtraction.lean:301`) applied to any Čech representative of the class, and
173	`relPicMk_surjective` supplies the representative.  So the existential
174	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre` asks for is met outright, with no choice left to the caller.
175	
176	This is the statement `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre.lean`'s header names as not claimed, and it
177	too is `GeometricallyReduced`-free. -/
178	theorem exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
179	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A))
180	    (hμ : ∃ z : relPic C (overSpec k A), relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k A) z = μ) :
181	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π, IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D := by
182	  obtain ⟨z, rfl⟩ := hμ
183	  obtain ⟨L₀, rfl⟩ := relPicMk_surjective C (overSpec k A) z
184	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq
185	    (C := C) (B := A) (π := π) L₀
186	  exact ⟨D, isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt C π L₀ D hD⟩
187	
188	/-! ## The honesty hypothesis, and why it is not vacuous -/
189	
190	variable (C) in
191	/-- **The honesty hypothesis: `μ` is a plus unit on every affine piece of the test.**
192	
193	This is the one thing the producer needs of `μ`, and it is a genuine hypothesis rather than a
194	restatement: a plus class over `Spec A` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E`, and
195	`Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean` is the record that it becomes honest over `E.Carrier` and not over
196	`A`.  So `IsPlusHonest` is exactly the gap between an arbitrary class and one the producer reaches.
197	
198	It is stated per affine piece because that is the shape `isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre` consumes;
199	over an affine test it is the single condition that `μ` is in the range of `relPicToPicEt`. -/
200	def IsPlusHonest (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (μ : picEt C T) : Prop :=
201	  ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens, ∃ z : relPic C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)),
202	    relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)) z
203	      = picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) μ
204	
205	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] in
206	variable (C) in
207	/-- Honesty is closed under multiplication — the range of `relPicToPicEt` is a subgroup, and
208	`picEtMap` is a homomorphism. -/
209	theorem IsPlusHonest.mul {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {μ ν : picEt C T}
210	    (hμ : IsPlusHonest C T μ) (hν : IsPlusHonest C T ν) :
211	    IsPlusHonest C T (μ * ν) := by
212	  intro U
213	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hμ U
214	  obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := hν U
215	  exact ⟨z * w, by rw [map_mul, hz, hw, map_mul]⟩
216	
217	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] in
218	variable (C) in
219	/-- Honesty is closed under inversion. -/
220	theorem IsPlusHonest.inv {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {μ : picEt C T}
221	    (hμ : IsPlusHonest C T μ) :
222	    IsPlusHonest C T μ⁻¹ := by
223	  intro U
224	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hμ U
225	  exact ⟨z⁻¹, by rw [map_inv, hz, map_inv]⟩
226	
227	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] in
228	variable (C) in
229	/-- Honesty is closed under powers. -/
230	theorem IsPlusHonest.pow {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {μ : picEt C T}
231	    (hμ : IsPlusHonest C T μ) (m : ℕ) :
232	    IsPlusHonest C T (μ ^ m) := by
233	  intro U
234	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hμ U
235	  exact ⟨z ^ m, by rw [map_pow, hz, map_pow]⟩
236	
237	variable (C) in
238	/-- **A θ-family is honest at every test** — the first half of the non-vacuity check.
239	
240	`thetaFamily_natural` restricts a θ-family to a θ-family, and `thetaFamily_overSpec_affineEquiv`
241	says its affine collapse is the plus unit of the base-changed base class.  So a θ-family is in the
242	range of the unit on every affine piece, with no hypothesis on the curve.
243	
244	This is why `chartTwist` preserves honesty: two of its three factors are θ-families. -/
245	theorem thetaFamily_isPlusHonest (L₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic)
246	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
247	    IsPlusHonest C T (thetaFamily C L₀ T) := by
248	  intro U
249	  refine ⟨relPicAlgMap C (Algebra.ofId k Γ(T.left, U.1)) (relPicMk C (overSpec k k) L₀), ?_⟩
250	  rw [thetaFamily_natural]
251	  exact (picEtAffineEquiv C Γ(T.left, U.1)).injective (by
252	    rw [picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt, thetaFamily_overSpec_affineEquiv])
253	
254	variable (C) in
255	/-- A Σ-family is honest: it *is* a θ-family (`sigmaFamily` is defined as one). -/
256	theorem sigmaFamily_isPlusHonest (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
257	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
258	    IsPlusHonest C T (sigmaFamily C Z T) :=
259	  thetaFamily_isPlusHonest C _ T
260	
261	variable (C π) in
262	/-- **THE ABEL VALUE IS HONEST AT EVERY TEST** — the witness that carries weight, and the one this
263	file's header cited by name before it existed (see the header's own retraction).
264	
265	The θ- and Σ-family witnesses above are the *twist factors*, which `chartTwist_isPlusHonest`
266	discharges anyway; they say nothing about the class being charted.  Since
267	`chartValue = abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹` and honesty is a subgroup condition, honesty of a **chart
268	value** reduces to honesty of `abelDiv` — so this is the row that makes CHART-U(b) unconditional
269	on the classes DAT-C's Σ-chart actually reads.
270	
271	It is cheap for a structural reason: `abelDiv`'s components are `abelDivPlus`, i.e. `PicEtAff.unit`
272	of `relPicMk` of the family's class, and `relPicToPicEt`'s components are `PicEtAff.unit` of
273	`relPicMap` — so the witness on the piece `U` is the class of the *restricted* family, and
274	`abelDiv_val` plus `picEtMap_abelDiv` line the two up. -/
275	theorem abelDiv_isPlusHonest {n : ℕ} (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
276	    (s : divFamZar C π n T) :
277	    IsPlusHonest C T (abelDiv C π n T s) := by
278	  intro U
279	  refine ⟨relPicMk C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1))
280	    ((divFamZarAffineEquiv C π n Γ(T.left, U.1)
281	      (divFamZar.map C π n (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) s)).picClass), ?_⟩
282	  rw [picEtMap_abelDiv, abelDiv_overSpec]
283	  rfl
284	
285	variable (C) in
286	/-- **`chartTwist` PRESERVES honesty** — the reason the producer reaches the Σ-chart.
287	
288	`chartTwist λ = λ · θᵐ · Σ⁻¹`, and both twist factors are θ-families, hence honest at every test
289	with no hypothesis.  Since honesty is a subgroup condition, the twisted class is honest exactly
290	when `λ` is.
291	
292	So the residue of CHART-U(b) is **the λ-factor alone**: no twist bookkeeping enters, which is the
293	mis-pricing the §3.3 correction 5 records. -/
294	theorem chartTwist_isPlusHonest (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
295	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) {lam : picEt C T} (hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam) :
296	    IsPlusHonest C T (chartTwist C m Z T lam) := by
297	  rw [chartTwist]
298	  exact (hlam.mul C ((thetaFamily_isPlusHonest C (thetaCechClass C) T).pow C m)).mul C
299	    ((sigmaFamily_isPlusHonest C Z T).inv C)
300	
301	/-! ## CHART-U(b) with the residue discharged -/
302	
303	set_option linter.overlappingInstances false in
304	variable (C π) in
305	/-- **CHART-U(b) AT A GENERAL TEST, WITH NO RESIDUE**, for a class that is honest on the affine
306	pieces of the test.
307	
308	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre` needs a per-piece datum with the plus-class property;
309	`exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range` produces one from honesty, and
310	`chartTwist_isPlusHonest` says the twist does not disturb honesty.  So the whole chain — the
311	engine, RE-5, the dictionary, the fibre-field invariance, `haff`, the presentation, `hconv`,
312	`hplus`, and now the producer — closes on the single hypothesis `IsPlusHonest`.
313	
314	`IsAffineHom π` follows from `IsFinite π`, whence the disabled overlapping-instance linter — the
315	same configuration `chartLocusAffineLocal_of_plusFibre` carries and for the same reason. -/
316	theorem isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest
317	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
318	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
319	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) (hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam) :
320	    IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z lam) :=
321	  isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre C π hπ m Z T lam fun U =>
322	    exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range C π _
323	      (by
324	        obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := chartTwist_isPlusHonest C m Z T hlam U
325	        exact ⟨z, hz.trans (picEtMap_chartTwist m Z (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam)⟩)
326	
327	set_option linter.overlappingInstances false in
328	variable (C π) in
329	/-- **The chart locus as an OPEN OF THE TEST, from honesty alone** — the shape the `W` field of a
330	chart datum consumes (`chartLocusOpens`, `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:115`), with its `haff`
331	argument discharged rather than passed through.
332	
333	This is c9b's clause (i) paid in full for an honest class: not "reduced to", but produced. -/
334	def chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest
335	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
336	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
337	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) (hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam) :
338	    T.left.Opens where
339	  carrier := chartLocus C m Z lam
340	  is_open' := isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest C π hπ m Z T lam hlam
341	
342	@[simp]
343	lemma mem_chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest
344	    {hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom}
345	    {m : ℕ} {Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor}
346	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} {hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam}
347	    {t : T.left} :
348	    t ∈ chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest C π hπ m Z T lam hlam ↔ t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam :=
349	  Iff.rfl
350	
351	end
352	
353	end AlgebraicGeometry

13	clauses mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative` actually conjoins, and gives a criterion whose
14	input is elementwise.  This file instantiates that criterion at the Abel chart and at
15	`V := chartLocus`, which is the pair `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
16	
17	The point is to make the residue **one named clause about the chart locus** instead of the
18	whole certificate.  Concretely, the criterion's `ChartFibrePresented` datum has four fields,
19	and at the Abel chart three of them are supplied here:
20	
21	| field | at the Abel chart | status |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `W` | `chartLocus` of the test point's class, as an open | **shape supplied here**, but at the
24	  cost of `haff` — see the retraction below |
25	| `r` | the divisor family over the locus | the classifier `divRepClassifyZar` |
26	| `sq` | its class is the test's class | the classifier's own characterisation |
27	| `exists_factor` | uniqueness of the normalized representative | **the relative form of GAP-2** |
28	
29	So `W` needs only B-4 (**not** "nothing" — retracted below), `sq` is a property of whatever
30	`r` is, and the genuine content is
31	concentrated in `r` (a construction, from the classifier) and `exists_factor` (relative
32	GAP-2).  This file makes that split machine-checkable: `IsChartLocusFibre` below names
33	exactly the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple **at the chart locus**, and
34	`isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` proves `IsChartUniv` from it.
35	
36	## Why this is not a restatement
37	
38	A reduction that merely renames its obligation is worthless, and this one is checked against
39	that failure mode in two directions:
40	
41	* `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised, so the `W` field is a *shape* a lane
42	  no longer has to invent.
43	
44	  **RETRACTED 2026-07-29, second clause only** (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`).  This
45	  read "the `W` field costs zero, which is a real reduction of the datum from four fields to
46	  three".  The cost is not zero: `chartLocusOpens` takes the argument `haff`, and **nothing in
47	  the tree discharges it**.  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` removed the
48	  `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` hypothesis but passes `haff` straight through, as does
49	  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` before it; the affine case that would feed it
50	  (`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation`) is itself conditional on
51	  `IsChartDatumPresentation`, which is dat-b row B-4's named residue and is only half landed.
52	  So the datum went from four fields to three *shapes* but not to three *obligations*.  The
53	  residue is now named `ChartLocusAffineLocal` and reduced to B-4's own obligation by
54	  `chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation`;
55	* `isChartLocusFibre_of_isChartUniv` is the **converse**: `IsChartUniv` at the chart locus
56	  gives injectivity on every test, so a lane cannot obtain `IsChartUniv` while avoiding the
57	  content of `exists_factor`.  The reduction is therefore an equivalence in the direction
58	  that matters, not a weakening.
59	
60	## Main declarations
61	
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusOpens` — `chartLocus` as an honest `T.Opens`, using the
63	  unconditional general-test openness.  This is the `V` that `restrictChart` wants.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsChartLocusFibre` — the residue: the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple
65	  of the criterion, at the chart locus, for every test point.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` — **the reduction**: that triple
67	  gives `IsChartUniv` (hence the `hf` of the `(f, hf)` pair) at any open.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_of_isChartUniv` — the converse-direction check.
69	-/

171	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
172	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
173	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z

175	    (h : IsChartLocusFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg) (V : D.left.Opens) :
176	    IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V :=
177	  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart V
178	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented _ fun T g => (h T g).some)

191	theorem injective_of_isChartUniv {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
192	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
193	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
194	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
195	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
196	    (V : D.left.Opens) (h : IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
